questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize that nothing had to be invented mid-incident?
options: Every mechanism used already existed from earlier lessons — building the process in advance means an incident is spent running it, not designing it under pressure
The incident described in this lesson was entirely hypothetical with no real mechanisms involved
Improvising a new process mid-incident is always the better approach
This lesson introduces several brand-new concepts not covered elsewhere in the chapter
questions.explain: An incident is the worst possible time to be designing a process instead of running one.

questions.q: In the walkthrough, what was the actual resolution, as distinct from the mitigation?
options: Updating the CI pipeline to validate Eventstream definitions, preventing this specific mistake from recurring — not the rollback itself
The canary rollback that restored correct dashboard numbers
The Activator alert firing in the first place
Posting a status update saying the issue was being investigated
questions.explain: Resolution is the slower, carefully-done fix that prevents recurrence — the rollback was only mitigation.

questions.q: Why did the walkthrough conclude this incident was NOT a disaster, per Lesson 59's distinction?
options: The system was never down or unreachable — it was producing wrong numbers, which calls for incident response, not disaster recovery
Disasters are defined purely by how severe the numbers looked
Any Sev 1 alert automatically counts as a disaster
It was actually a disaster, just handled using incident-response tools instead
questions.explain: Correctly recognizing what an incident isn't avoids wasting time on the wrong playbook.

questions.q: What happened to the error budget (Lesson 56) as a result of this incident?
options: 12 minutes of degraded freshness was debited from the month's error budget
The error budget was fully reset back to its maximum
The SLO itself was permanently loosened after the incident
Error budgets don't apply to incidents caused by a deployment
questions.explain: This ties the incident directly back to Lesson 56's concept of the error budget as a spendable, trackable resource.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what happens if you "take away" any single mechanism from this chapter during the incident?
options: The whole response breaks down at that point — e.g., without severity tiers the alert doesn't reach anyone appropriately, without a runbook the on-call engineer starts from zero
Nothing changes — each lesson's mechanism is fully redundant with the others
Only the final write-up would be affected, nothing earlier in the response
The incident would resolve itself automatically regardless
questions.explain: Every lesson in the chapter is one gear in the same machine — this incident is what makes that visible all at once.
